findings.explanation: ACE inhibitor plus ARB (dual renin-angiotensin blockade) is an additive/synergistic effect, as the record's own mechanismNote says ('Additive blockade of the same hormone system'). 'Antagonism' means opposing effects, so the mechanism label contradicts the note and misdescribes the pair (the label is correct for metformin-prednisolone). The same wrong label is on interactions/lisinopril-aliskiren (note: 'Dual renin-angiotensin blockade'), interactions/losartan-ace-inhibitors-class and interactions/lisinopril-arbs-class.
findings.suggestedFix: On all four records change the mechanism to 'other' (or 'additive hypotension' / 'hyperkalaemia risk') and keep the 'additive blockade' note.

findings.quote: MedlinePlus: Azithromycin precautions (doses may need changing or monitoring with these medicines)
findings.explanation: The MONITOR_OR_ADJUST tier is taken from a generic US MedlinePlus sentence about azithromycin, not from UK wording for this pair. UK citalopram labelling and MHRA advice (2011 Drug Safety Update) say citalopram/escitalopram should not be used with other QT-prolonging medicines (the SmPC lists this as a contraindication), azithromycin is a recognised QT-prolonging macrolide, and the record's own action ('an alternative antibiotic where possible') is an avoid-type statement. 'Monitor or adjust' therefore understates the UK position for a pair the checker shows to the public. None of the three references is specific to citalopram.
findings.suggestedFix: Re-derive the tier from the BNF interaction text and the citalopram SmPC (likely AVOID_COMBINATION, at minimum SPECIALIST_OR_CLOSE_MONITORING); add the BNF citalopram interactions page or the MHRA citalopram QT Drug Safety Update as a reference; if the tier is kept, state why the UK position is weaker than avoid.

findings.quote: Strong CYP3A4 inhibition; the BNF gives erythromycin the same dose-limit-or-avoid advice as clarithromycin
findings.explanation: Erythromycin is a moderate, not strong, CYP3A4 inhibitor; in atorvastatin prescribing information it raises atorvastatin exposure by only about a third, whereas clarithromycin raises it roughly 4-fold (the clarithromycin record's own figure). The effect sentence copied into this record ('Clarithromycin and erythromycin raise atorvastatin levels several-fold') therefore overstates erythromycin, and the claim that the BNF gives identical advice for both macrolides is not evident from the cited pages.
findings.suggestedFix: Describe erythromycin as a moderate CYP3A4 (and OATP1B1) inhibitor, give this record its own effect sentence without 'several-fold', and keep 'same advice as clarithromycin' and the tier only if the BNF text confirms it.

findings.quote: Erythromycin, azole antifungals and other strong CYP3A4 inhibitors
findings.explanation: Erythromycin is a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor; the strong ones are clarithromycin, itraconazole, ketoconazole and boosted HIV regimens. The perpetrator field repeats 'Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors'. Also the effect sentence names clarithromycin but bAgents omits it (a separate pair record exists).
findings.suggestedFix: Say 'CYP3A4 inhibitors (for example erythromycin, itraconazole, ketoconazole)' without 'strong'.

findings.quote: Official UK advice: pause the statin during fusidic acid and for 7 days after.
findings.explanation: Worded as an instruction to stop a medicine. The MHRA/SmPC advice is addressed to prescribers (avoid the combination; if systemic fusidic acid is essential, the statin is withheld by the prescriber), and an educational page should describe it. A reader could act on it unsupervised. Identical wording in interactions/rosuvastatin-fusidic-acid.
findings.suggestedFix: 'UK regulators advise that systemic fusidic acid and statins are not used together; where fusidic acid is essential the prescriber withholds the statin during treatment and for 7 days after the last dose.'

findings.quote: Official UK information: count every product; no more than 4 g in 24 hours for an adult.
findings.explanation: A maximum daily dose framed as an instruction, with no qualifier. 4 g in 24 hours is the usual adult ceiling, but UK labelling gives lower limits for people under 50 kg and for liver disease, chronic alcohol use or malnutrition, so 'for an adult' can be read as safe for everyone.
findings.suggestedFix: 'The usual adult maximum is 4 g in 24 hours across all products; lower limits apply with low body weight or liver problems.'

findings.quote: Avoid regular use where possible; monitor kidney function and potassium if combined.
findings.explanation: Unattributed imperative addressed to the reader, unlike the pair records that begin 'Official UK guidance:'. It reads as advice to an individual about an over-the-counter medicine. Identical wording in interactions/losartan-nsaids-class.
findings.suggestedFix: 'Official UK guidance: regular NSAID use is avoided where possible; if combined, kidney function and potassium are checked.'

findings.explanation: The effect text describes severe swelling of the face and airway, but nothing tells a reader that this is an emergency. Similar red-flag items are phrased only as 'report' (black stools in interactions/aspirin-sertraline and interactions/ibuprofen-sertraline) or 'signs of bleeding' (anticoagulant pairs).
findings.suggestedFix: Add urgent-care signposting, e.g. 'Swelling of the lips, face, tongue or throat, or difficulty breathing, needs emergency help (999)'; likewise 'black stools or vomiting blood need urgent medical help'.

findings.quote: Iodinated contrast (allergy and kidney precautions; metformin paused)
findings.explanation: Unqualified 'metformin paused' conflicts with interactions/metformin-iodinated-contrast, which says metformin is withheld in people with reduced kidney function. UK practice (BNF, Royal College of Radiologists) is not to stop metformin routinely for contrast when kidney function is normal.
findings.suggestedFix: 'Iodinated contrast (allergy and kidney precautions; metformin may need pausing in people with reduced kidney function)'.

findings.quote: no dose limit in kidney impairment
findings.explanation: The atorvastatin SmPC needs no renal dose adjustment, but NICE starts atorvastatin at 20 mg in chronic kidney disease and advises agreeing higher doses with a renal specialist when eGFR is below 30, so 'no dose limit' can be read as unrestricted. It also sits beside '80 mg for secondary prevention', which is not the NICE dose in CKD.
findings.suggestedFix: 'no renal dose adjustment in the SmPC; NICE advises specialist input before higher doses when eGFR is below 30'.

findings.quote: Rises within 6 hours, peaks at about 48 hours, falls quickly (half-life about 19 hours)
findings.explanation: The only references are two short US consumer pages from MedlinePlus. They cannot plausibly support the CRP kinetics above, the 'point-of-care antibiotic decisions' use (a UK NICE-guided practice) or ESR age/sex reference limits. 'No diagnostic threshold' (Units and range row) also sits oddly beside point-of-care CRP cut-offs used in NICE antibiotic guidance. The facts themselves are standard.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a UK source (NICE NG138 for point-of-care CRP, or a laboratory-medicine reference) or remove the specific kinetic figures; qualify 'no diagnostic threshold' as 'no fixed diagnostic cut-off'.

findings.quote: the BNF advises caution or avoidance depending on the drug.
findings.explanation: The record says the BNF may advise avoidance for some partner drugs, yet one tier (MONITOR_OR_ADJUST) and a US MedlinePlus severitySource are applied to all of them, including amiodarone, sotalol and quinolones, where UK sources are stricter than 'doses may need changing'. Wording and tier disagree, and for a UK-first site the tier should follow the BNF per partner.
findings.suggestedFix: Split higher-risk partners (amiodarone, sotalol) into their own pair records with BNF-derived tiers, or raise the tier and cite the BNF as severitySource.

findings.quote: ACE inhibitors can enhance the glucose-lowering effect of diabetes medicines such as metformin, insulin and sulfonylureas, occasionally causing low blood sugar in the first weeks.
findings.explanation: The class wording in labelling concerns hypoglycaemia mainly with insulin and sulfonylureas; metformin on its own does not cause hypoglycaemia, so a pair record titled lisinopril-metformin with mechanism 'additive hypoglycaemia risk' probably overstates this pair. I could not confirm that the cited NHS/BNF pages name metformin.
findings.suggestedFix: Anchor the record to insulin/sulfonylureas, or reword to say metformin alone rarely causes low blood sugar; confirm the BNF wording.

notes: 79 records read in full (72 interactions, 7 comparisons); 13 findings (0 high, 3 medium, 10 low), well under the 20 cap. The set is largely accurate and UK-consistent: dose limits, washout periods (36 h, 7 days, 48 h, 3 days), contraindications and mechanisms checked out, and US wording is labelled as US. Not reported because I could not confirm without sources: (a) the dose caps 'atorvastatin 10 mg with ciclosporin' and 'rosuvastatin 10 mg with gemfibrozil' (UK atorvastatin labelling may say avoid with ciclosporin) - please check against current BNF/SmPC; these two records are therefore not listed as clean; (b) whether the cited MHRA Drug Safety Update (titled for atorvastatin) covers fusidic acid with rosuvastatin; (c) https://www.nhs.uk/medicines/aspirin/ is cited in seven aspirin records, whereas NHS normally has separate 'aspirin for pain relief' and 'low-dose aspirin' pages - link check advised. Observations: the lithium pairs (ACE inhibitor/ARB/NSAID) sit at MONITOR_OR_ADJUST although their action text says 'avoid where possible' and lithium has a narrow therapeutic index, while methotrexate pairs are SPECIALIST_OR_CLOSE_MONITORING - consider consistency; duplication records say 'it never combines' / 'guidance never combines them' (atorvastatin-rosuvastatin, azithromycin-macrolides), absolutes the cited pages do not state; amlodipine-simvastatin 'roughly doubles' is slightly high (labelling gives about 1.6-1.8-fold). The scratch text files I used to read the slices were deleted; only this findings file remains.
